  of the CEQA guidelines. Based on Staff’s analysis, the request to reduce the required parking for
  the expansion to an existing restaurant will not result in any changes in land use and will not have a
  significant effect on the environment; thereby staff feels that the project qualifies for this exemption.

  SUGGESTED ACTION: Conduct Public Hearing. We recommend approving Case No.

  A motion was made by Vice Chairmember Rodriguez, seconded by Commissioner Roman, to
  approve recommendation and adopt Resolution No. 2021­006 with the following conditions, that
  events in access of 40 or more people may only be held on weekends before 2pm and shall not
  exceed 2 hours..

  The motion was carried by the following vote:

  AYES: 4; Roman, Winford, Navarro, Rodriguez
  NOES: 0;
  ABSENT: 1; Hernandez
  RECUSE: 0;

  Motion carried: 4–0–1–0

Chairman Winford read the title and recommendation into record and requests a staff report.

Kevin Nguyen, Associate Planner II gives a staff report presentation utilizing PowerPoint.

Planning Commissioner Roman speaks and inquired about Number of parking available during peak
hours.

Chairman Winford speaks and inquires to staff about parking spaces, seasons where the tax business
is at peak hours and requires more spaces, seasonal food takeout orders and if it requires more
parking, and will the lot still meet ADA parking requirements, re­striping stalls or reconfiguring
requirements. He also asked about slightly reduced table occupancy.

Kevin Ngyuen, Associate Planner II speaks and states that the proposed request will result in 50% less
parking.and addresses all of Chairman Winford’s inquiries.

Commissioner Roman spoke and asked a question about a lane expansion being done along Carson
Street He asked if this would impact Julian’s business. He also inquired about handicap space
additions due to this request.

Chairman Winford then opens the Public Hearing at 6:26pm and asks the applicant to state name &
address into record.

Charles Lawrence, stated his name and identified himself as the owner of Julian’s Mexican Foods.He
also spoke and expounded upon the reasons for the restaurant’s dining room expansion desires which
would reduce parking spaces. It would enable them to host parties and different events. They will also
be applying for a beer and wine license.

Commissioner Navarro spoke and asked if the liquor license would effect their hours of business.

Charles Lawrence, stated his name and identified himself as the owner of Julian’s Mexican Foods.He
also spoke and expounded upon the reasons for the restaurant’s dining room expansion desires which
would reduce parking spaces. It would enable them to host parties and different events. They will also
be applying for a beer and wine license.

Commissioner Navarro spoke and asked if the liquor license would effect their hours of business.

Commissioner Roman spoke and thanked Mr. Lawrence for his business in the city and wished him well.

Vice Chair Rodriguez spoke about events taking up more space on the weekends and limiting space for
laundry customers. She also inquired about parking space designation for each business.

Kevin Nguyen, Associate Planner II and Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attorney both spoke and
explained that the city at this time does not have the authority to designate spaces.

Charles Lawrence, Owner of Julian’s Mexican Foods stated for the record that if his dining expansion
and parking reduction project proposes an issue for residents at night, that he will not conduct business
during the night.

Commissioner Navarro also spoke and expressed her concerns regarding single mom patrons being
affected by the project.

Chairman Winford spoke and expressed his concerns about the number of cars present as a result of
this project proposing future issues. He asked about Maximum Occupancy of the restaurant as it relates
to the Conditional Use Permit.

Kevin Nguyen , Associate Planner II spoke and explained that the inspectors and building officials
determine the maximum occupancy.

Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attorney spoke and addressed the conditions and potential issues
relative to parking spaces and how restaurant occupancy may effect it.

Charles Lawrence, Owner of Julian’s Mexican Foods spoke and stated that he would not allow parties to
be booked.

Vice Chair Rodriguez spoke and inquired about parking that overflows onto streets. She also suggested
that 2 hour limits be set for large parties to control parking.

Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attorney spoke and expounded upon the idea of have a 2 hour parking
limit for events as a condition added to this resolution.

Chairman Winford closed the Public Hearing at 7:28pm

  SUGGESTED ACTION: Approve Recommendation.

C.  DISCUSSION ITEM(S)

There were no Discussion items.

D.  ORAL STAFF REPORT(S)

1.  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT STATUS REPORT

  Kevin Nguyen, Associate Planner II presented the Planning Commission with 11 items on a
  Development Project Status Report.as requested by Chairman Winford in a previous meeting.

E.  CITY ATTORNEY REPORT(S)

There were no City Attorney reports.

F.  ORAL COMMISSIONER REPORT(S)

Chairman Winford spoke and exclaimed that he loves the Planning Commission Staff, Kevin, Associate
Planner II and Shavon Moore – Cage, Planning Secretary. He would also like to make sure that the
Planning Commission receives the reports related to Planning that goes to Council. He would like to
receive them on a regular basis.

G.  ADJOURNMENT

Chairman Winford adjourned the meeting at 7:38pm to the next Planning Commission Meeting on
Wednesday, June 9, 2021.
